verdict.rationale: Cursor Automations run cloud agents in the background on a recurring schedule, and scheduled triggers accept preset options or a cron expression. Automations can be created in the Agents Window, at cursor.com/automations, or by describing the workflow in plain language with the /automate skill, so this is a recurring schedule rather than a one-off action. The homepage repeats the claim of always-on agents that run on schedules. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that scheduled automations run reliably, and documentation of schedule management such as run history, pausing, or failure handling.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can schedule recurring jobs or workflows

citations.quote: Cursor Automations run cloud agents in the background, either on a schedule or in response to events from GitHub, GitLab, Slack, webhooks, Linear, and more.
Scheduled triggers take "preset options or ... a cron expression"
Set up always-on agents that run on schedules or triggers to build, maintain, and fix your software.
The `/automate` skill lets you describe the workflow you want in plain language. Cursor configures the automation's triggers, instructions, and tools for you.
